title.en: Draft a story with a twist

es: Escribir una historia breve con hábito, antecedente, giro, condicional y una frase contada.

teaching.en: Every Saturday, Sara used to walk past an old shop.
teaching.es: Cada sábado, Sara solía pasar delante de una tienda vieja.
teaching.explanationEs: Used to + verbo base presenta la rutina al empezar la historia.
teaching.audioText: Every Saturday, Sara used to walk past an old shop.

teaching.en: One day, she found a camera which her grandfather had lost years before.
teaching.es: Un día encontró una cámara que su abuelo había perdido años antes.
teaching.explanationEs: Had + participio: lo que había pasado antes del hecho principal.
segments: One day, she found a camera which
her grandfather had lost years before.
teaching.audioText: One day, she found a camera which her grandfather had lost years before.

teaching.en: Suddenly, she saw her own face in a photo. That was the twist.
teaching.es: De repente, vio su propia cara en una foto. Ese fue el giro.
teaching.explanationEs: Suddenly abre el giro; se usa con un pasado simple (saw).
segments: Suddenly, she saw her own face in
a photo. That was the twist.
teaching.audioText: Suddenly, she saw her own face in a photo. That was the twist.

teaching.en: If she had not entered the shop, she would never have found it.
teaching.es: Si no hubiera entrado en la tienda, nunca lo habría encontrado.
teaching.explanationEs: If + had + participio, would have + participio: lo que pudo pasar.
segments: If she had not entered the shop,
she would never have found it.
teaching.audioText: If she had not entered the shop, she would never have found it.

teaching.en: She told her mother that it was the best surprise of her life.
teaching.es: Le dijo a su madre que era la mejor sorpresa de su vida.
teaching.explanationEs: Told + persona + that: una frase contada dentro de la historia.
segments: She told her mother that it was
the best surprise of her life.
teaching.audioText: She told her mother that it was the best surprise of her life.

teaching.en: The ending gives a lesson: a small habit can change a life.
teaching.es: El final da una lección: un pequeño hábito puede cambiar una vida.
teaching.explanationEs: El final cierra con una reflexión.
segments: The ending gives a lesson: a
small habit can change a life.
teaching.audioText: The ending gives a lesson: a small habit can change a life.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué frase presentarías la rutina del personaje al empezar la historia?

choices.text: Every morning, Leo had walked to school.
Every morning, Leo used to walk to school.
Every morning, Leo would have walked to school.

feedback.es: La rutina pasada se presenta con used to + verbo base. Had walked cuenta un hecho anterior y would have walked es una hipótesis.

prompt.es: Completa: «Encontró una carta que su madre había escrito.»

feedback.es: Un antecedente lleva had + participio: had written (write, wrote, written).

hint.es: Hecho anterior: had + participio de write.

origin.text: She found a letter that her mother had ___.

prompt.es: Ordena: «De repente, se apagaron las luces.»

feedback.es: Suddenly abre el giro y el hecho va en pasado simple: the lights went out.

hint.es: El conector del giro va primero.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada conector con su función en la historia.

pairs.es: abre una reflexión sobre lo que pudo pasar

feedback.es: Cada conector marca una parte de la historia: rutina, giro, hipótesis y final.

pairs.es: abre una reflexión sobre lo que pudo pasar

prompt.es: Escucha y elige el giro de esta historia.

choices.text: Leo stopped playing in the park.
A girl taught Leo a new song.
A girl knew a song that he had never taught.

feedback.es: El giro es inesperado: la niña cantó la canción sin error y Leo no se la había enseñado a nadie.

origin.audio: Every Friday, Leo used to play his guitar in the park. One day, a girl sat next to him and sang his song without a mistake. He had never taught it to anyone.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si hubiera salido antes, habría visto el final.»

feedback.es: En la segunda parte del tercer condicional se usa would have + participio.

origin.text: If I had left earlier, I would ___ seen the end.

prompt.es: Escribe una historia corta: rutina, antecedente, giro, hipótesis y una frase contada.

answer.text: Every evening, Leo used to walk his dog in the park. One day, he found a bag which a woman had lost. Suddenly, the woman ran to him and smiled. It was her bag! If Leo had stayed at home, he would never have met her. She told him that she was very happy.
accepted: Every evening, Leo used to walk his dog in the park. One day, he found a bag which a woman had lost. Suddenly, the woman ran to him and smiled. It was her bag! If Leo had stayed at home, he would never have met her. She told him that she was very happy.

Leo used to walk his dog in the park every evening. One day, he found a bag that a woman had lost. Suddenly, the woman ran to him and smiled: it was her bag! If Leo had stayed at home, he would never have met her. She told him that she was very happy.

Every evening, Leo used to walk his dog in the park. One day, he found a bag that a woman had lost. Suddenly, the woman ran to him and smiled. It was her bag! If he had stayed at home, he would never have met her. She said that she was very happy.

feedback.es: La historia sigue el orden del relato: rutina (used to), antecedente (had lost), giro (suddenly), hipótesis (if + had + participio, would have) y una frase contada (told him that).

origin.text: Datos: cada tarde, Leo solía pasear a su perro por el parque. Un día encontró una bolsa que una mujer había perdido. De repente, la mujer corrió hacia él y sonrió: ¡era su bolsa! Si Leo se hubiera quedado en casa, nunca la habría conocido. Ella le dijo que estaba muy feliz.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es el giro de esta historia?

choices.text: The neighbour had baked the same cake years before.
Mia gave a cake to her neighbour.

feedback.es: El giro es lo inesperado: la vecina ya había hecho ese mismo pastel. La rutina de Mia y el regalo son la base de la historia.

origin.text: Mia used to bake bread every Sunday. One day, she made a cake for her neighbour. Suddenly, the neighbour smiled: she had baked the same cake forty years before.

prompt.es: Completa las tres frases con la forma que falta.

feedback.es: Used to para la costumbre, had already para el antecedente y would have helped para la hipótesis: tres herramientas de la historia.

sentences: Every winter, my aunt ___ to make soup.
When I arrived, the film ___ already started.
If he had asked, she ___ have helped him.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Mi abuelo me contó que había vivido allí.»

answer.text: My grandfather told me that he had lived there

feedback.es: Told me that + oración: el verbo retrocede un paso y se cuenta con had lived.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase es una reflexión sobre lo que pudo pasar?

choices.text: Tom used to call us every night.
If Tom had called, we would have waited.
Tom had called before we arrived.

feedback.es: La reflexión usa if + had + participio y would have + participio. Las otras dos cuentan una costumbre y un antecedente.

prompt.es: Escribe el giro: de repente, Ana vio a su hermano en la foto.

answer.text: Suddenly, Ana saw her brother in the photo.
accepted: Suddenly, Ana saw her brother in the photo.
Suddenly Ana saw her brother in the photo.
Suddenly, she saw her brother in the photo.

feedback.es: El giro se abre con suddenly y el hecho va en pasado simple: saw her brother in the photo.

origin.text: Giro: de repente, Ana vio a su hermano en la foto.

prompt.es: Completa: «La historia tiene un final feliz.»

feedback.es: El ending es la parte que cierra la historia y puede traer una lección.
